profile.headline: Software Engineer at EControls
profile.summary:
Chief Electrical Engineer @ Purdue Electric Racing ‘21-‘22
Software Engineer at EControls

positions.title: Chief Electrical Engineer
positions.description:
- Oversaw high level team operations with regard to electrical subsystems.
- Worked with project management software to ensure tasks were started and completed on time while offering technical design effort where required to push tasks to completion.
- Re-tooled a custom BMS around the silicon shortage, while also expanding the architecture to accomodate future vehicles.

positions.title: Electronics Lead
positions.description:
- Oversaw day to day operations of the electronics subteam.
- Managed a small team of  ~15 dedicated individuals on integration of a 450V battery with an EmDrive H300 motor controller into the PER '20 vehicle.
- Worked on a refresh of our custom BMS to decrease current consumption, add proper isolation for signal integrity and noise immunity, and construct embedded and PC software for BMS control and live data viewing.

positions.title: Electronics Team Member
positions.description:
- Worked on multiple embedded software engineering tasks on the STM platform for PER's high performance EV. 
- Developed a lap timer with accompanying software for precise trackside timing in all environments. Worked on data management and routing via the vehicle's dual CAN bus networks. 
- Developed low level drivers for specific ICs, and wrote embedded software for PER's custom, in house BMS.

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description:
- Designed, built, and tested a digitally controlled battery sim capable of over 500W of output power.
- Updated UI to include specific animations while decoupling UI elements for proper operation over the entire lineup of battery based products.
- Updated internal libraries to ensure simple and reliable integration with MCU peripherals.

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description:
- Wrote and tested BMS software to provide open wire detection and overcharge/overdischarge protection.
- Debugged and tested software to ensure proper working operation at all times.
- Updated UI to give users a better insight as to current pack state.

positions.title: Information Technology Intern
positions.description:
- Worked on diagnosing and repairing equipment. 
- Wrote scripts to automate tasks.
- Interacted with individuals to help fix issues.

positions.title: Service Assistant
positions.description:
- Assisted customers with aircraft fueling to ensure on time departure.
- Helped airport staff fix computer based technology, as well as general tasks involving aviation to ensure proper FAA rules and regulations were being followed.

honors.title: FirstNet Hackathon: The Road to 5G: Third Place in "Best App for First Responders
honors.description: The FirstNet hackathon was an event centered around using technology to assist first responders in multiple ways. For our submission, we created an app to pair with a smart lock that would allow first responders quick entry into buildings and rooms when assistance is required. The app was built with react native and node.js and featured an iOS app with the capability of connecting to a server running on a Raspberry Pi. More information about the project can be found here: https://github.com/RyanSchw/Sentry_FirstNet
honors.issuer: Issued by FirstNet & AT&T Developer Programs · Sep 2019

honors.title: ENGR 131 Design Challenge Award
honors.description: This award was given for the design process and production of the HyperStation, a hyperlocal network of weather stations that teaches students how to program and Arduino while gathering useful weather data. It was given to for "outstanding performance in excellence in design produce and process".
honors.issuer: Issued by Professor Jennifer DeBoer · Dec 2018

projects.title: ENGR 131 Final Design Project - HyperStation
projects.description:
This project was designed to be a teaching tool to help underprivileged students in Tumaini, Kenya learn the basics of programming. This is accomplished through lesson plans that walk students through the basics of Arduino coding. This project is now being tweaked to alert farmers in Africa when weather conditions in certain regions are too bad to travel. This ongoing project is being continued as undergraduate research with the DeBoer lab at Purdue University. Currently, the goal of this project is to allow kids in Africa to learn programming while making a difference in their society.

This project won the ENGR 131 Design Challenge Award for "excellence in design product in process".
